definitions.explanation: A tunnel or passageway built underground for pedestrians to cross under roads, railways, or connect buildings.

examples.japanese: {地下道|ちかどう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{通|とお}って→通る：01243_tooru⟧⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}かう→向かう：01186_mukau⟧。
examples.english: I head to the station through the underground passage.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{地下道|ちかどう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦デパート→デパート：01022_depaato⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{結|むす}んでいる→結ぶ：02308_musubu⟧。
examples.english: This underground passage connects the station to the department store.
On rainy days, using the underground passage keeps you dry.

examples.japanese: {地下道|ちかどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}んでいる→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。

⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{暑|あつ}い→暑い：00619_atsui⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{地下道|ちかどう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{通|とお}る→通る：01243_tooru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{涼|すず}しくて→涼しい：00674_suzushii⟧⟦{助|たす}かる→助かる：01956_tasukaru⟧。
examples.english: On hot summer days, it's a relief to walk through the underground passage where it's cool.

notes:
COMPOSITION: ⟦{地下|ちか}→地下：03429_chika⟧ (underground) + ⟦{道|どう}→道：noentry⟧ (road, passage)

TYPES OF UNDERGROUND PASSAGES:
・⟦{歩行者|ほこうしゃ}→歩行者：03152_hokousha⟧⟦{専用|せんよう}→専用：12385_senyou⟧{地下道|ちかどう} - pedestrian-only underpass
・⟦{地下街|ちかがい}→地下街：09390_chikagai⟧ - underground shopping arcade (larger, with many shops)
・⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧{地下道|ちかどう} - station underground passage

ADVANTAGES:
・⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{濡|ぬ}れない→濡れる：00800_nureru⟧ - stay dry from rain
・⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{涼|すず}しい→涼しい：00674_suzushii⟧ - cool in summer
・⟦{信号|しんごう}→信号：03258_shingou⟧⟦{待|ま}ち→待つ：00469_matsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ - no waiting at traffic lights

RELATED TERMS:
・⟦{歩道橋|ほどうきょう}→歩道橋：06494_hodoukyou⟧ - pedestrian overpass (above-ground alternative)
・⟦{地下鉄|ちかてつ}→地下鉄：01020_chikatetsu⟧ - subway (underground train)
・⟦{地下街|ちかがい}→地下街：09390_chikagai⟧ - underground shopping area

NOTE: Major Japanese cities like Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya have extensive underground passage networks connecting train stations, department stores, and office buildings.
